title: CHOOSER uses protein foundation models to discover functional Casλ homologs
summary: The CHOOSER framework fine-tuned ESM-2 protein-language-model representations for alignment-free CRISPR-Cas discovery and pre-crRNA self-processing predictions. It nominated 11 Casλ homologs, nearly doubling the known Casλ set. Wet-lab work on selected homologs confirmed pre-crRNA processing for five of six tested proteins; EphcCasλ also cleaved target DNA and showed trans-cleavage activity, with a TTR PAM reported.
ai_technology: CHOOSER, a protein foundation-model framework fine-tuning ESM-2 representations for Cas homolog identification and Cas12 pre-crRNA-processing classification
organization: Tongji University; Zhejiang Lab; Shanghai East Hospital; collaborating Chinese research institutions

evidence.tested: Wet-lab work on selected homologs confirmed pre-crRNA processing for five of six tested proteins; EphcCasλ also cleaved target DNA and showed trans-cleavage activity, with a TTR PAM reported.
evidence.unknown: This is a specific functional genomics result, not evidence of a ready-to-use diagnostic or gene-editing tool. Only selected candidates were purified and tested; the paper reports pre-crRNA activity in five of six tested Casλ proteins and DNA-cleavage validation for a subset. EphcCasλ activity and PAM characterization are in-vitro findings. The article has a publisher-listed author correction dated 2025-01-09; this record relies on the version-of-record text and retains limited scope.
evidence.ai_role: CHOOSER mined candidate proteins adjacent to CRISPR arrays using learned sequence representations rather than alignment-only detection and prioritized Cas12 homologs by predicted pre-crRNA processing. The study reported 11 Casλ homologs and experimentally tested selected predictions; purified EphcCasλ was validated for self-processing pre-crRNA, DNA cleavage and trans-cleavage.
